b719060d388bb124d9fbafda4cc18595927113e2.summary:
The app is built — a single self-contained `index.html` ("HackTube") that works end to end when opened in a browser.

What it does:

- **Curated HN canon as the dataset.** Since HN has no "videos" API dimension, the catalog is a hand-curated set of 41 videos that are genuinely re-submitted and re-recommended on Hacker News year after year — Bret Victor's "Inventing on Principle", Hamming's "You and Your Research", the Mother of All Demos, Rich Hickey's talks, Karpathy's GPT-from-scratch, "The Expert", KRAZAM's "Microservices", Ben Eater's 6502 build, and so on. Each entry carries title, speaker, year, duration, category, a description, an estimated HN mention count, and a "Why it's HN canon" note explaining its repeat-endorsement history.
- **Live HN data for the "repeat mentions" evidence.** On each watch page the app queries the Algolia HN Search API (CORS-enabled, no key needed) for real submissions of that video — matched by YouTube ID in the URL and by title — deduplicates them, filters to genuine matches, and lists the top threads with points, comment counts, date, and direct links to the `news.ycombinator.com` discussions, plus an "all HN results" search link. If the API is unreachable it degrades gracefully to a direct HN search link.
- **YouTube-style interface.** Dark theme, fixed header with search, category sidebar with per-category counts (Programming, Computer History, AI & ML, Science, Hardware, Talks, Tech & Society, Documentaries, Culture), sticky filter chips, sort control (most HN mentions / newest / oldest / A–Z), and a responsive card grid with real YouTube thumbnails, duration badges, and an "HN mentions" pill on every card.
- **Playback with context.** Clicking a card routes to `#/watch/<id>` (back button works) with an embedded `youtube-nocookie` player, metadata, the HN discussion panel, and a "More HN classics" related-videos rail that prioritizes the same category.

Everything runs from the one file — no build step, no dependencies — so it previews directly in a browser.
